claims.text: The FeCoNiCrAl coating deposited from 15–45 μm feedstock is below the required thickness.
The as-sprayed FeCoNiCrAl coating has a lamellar structure with inter-splat voids.
Post-deposition laser treatment can partially remelt the thermally sprayed splats.
Melting followed by coalescence can fuse deposited material into a continuous layer.
Laser remelting will eliminate inter-splat voids and densify the FeCoNiCrAl coating.
Laser remelting will improve inter-splat bonding and heal microstructural defects.
An argon atmosphere during laser remelting will prevent oxidation and preserve alloy integrity.
Densification by post-deposition laser remelting will produce an effectively thicker coating without adding material.
The laser-remelted coating will have a statistically significant thickness increase relative to the untreated 15–45 μm-feedstock coating.
Laser remelting will improve coating adhesion.
The laser-remelted coating will retain an intact, bond-coat-suitable microstructure.
The laser-remelted coating will have minimal oxidation relative to the untreated coating.
Standard APS or HVOF deposition with 15–45 μm feedstock produces a lamellar, porous, insufficiently thick coating that tends to oxidize.
Appropriate laser power density, scan speed, and spot size can achieve localized remelting without overheating, substrate dilution, or unwanted phase transformations.
Excessive laser energy can cause detrimental microstructural changes or substrate dilution.
The proposed treatment will remain effective under typical APS or HVOF processing conditions for FeCoNiCrAl coatings.
Compromising the inert environment may eliminate the treatment benefits.

contradictions.description: The proposed mechanism removes void volume and densifies a fixed amount of deposited material, which ordinarily contracts or preserves geometric thickness rather than increasing it. The predicted outcome and falsification test nevertheless require an increase in cross-sectional coating thickness, while no material-addition or redistribution mechanism is specified.
